title: disclosure.yaml, version 1
description: What a Home Assistant integration, card or app connects to and handles, as stated by its developer. Version 1 never changes; any change is a new version.

version.description: The version of this specification the file follows.

connections.description: Servers outside Home Assistant that the app contacts. An empty list says it contacts none.

links.description: Sites the app only links to. They open when a person selects the link.

pages.description: Pages and endpoints the app adds that answer without a Home Assistant login.

credentials.description: Passwords, tokens and keys the app asks the user for.

login_tokens.description: Home Assistant login tokens the app creates, reads or hands on. An empty list says it uses none.

home_assistant_access.description: Parts of Home Assistant the app uses beyond its own entities and settings. An empty list says it uses none.

embedded_keys.description: Keys, tokens and certificates written into the code the app ships.

telemetry.description: Usage statistics, analytics and crash reports. An empty list says the app sends none.

encoded_content.description: Large base64, hex or compressed content in the code.

compiled_code.description: Compiled files the app ships, such as native modules or Python bytecode. An empty list says it ships none.

runtime_downloads.description: Code the app downloads and runs while it runs. An empty list says it downloads none.

generated_files.description: Files the app writes outside its own storage.

host.description: A host name, optionally starting with *. for any subdomain, or an IP address.

destination.description: One host, or a list of hosts that share everything else in the entry.

destination_set_by.description: Who supplies the address when it isn't written in the code. setup: the user enters it while setting the app up. setting: a setting the user can change later. server_reply: a server's answer tells the app where to go next.

run_by.description: Who runs the server. developer: the app's developer. vendor: the company or public body whose device or service the app is for. third_party: anyone else, such as a map tile service. user: the user's own device or server.

component.description: Which integration, card or app in the repository the entry is about, by its domain or name. Only needed when the repository has more than one.

sends.description: What requests carry, beyond the request itself. An empty list says nothing more. ip_address: the user's IP address. physical_location: coordinates or a street address, of the home, a person or a device. map_area: the part of a map being viewed. entity_states: states or attributes of Home Assistant entities. credentials: a password, token or key the user gave. device_ids: serial numbers, MAC addresses or account ids of devices. ha_address: the address of the user's Home Assistant. media: camera images, audio or video. personal_details: a name, email address or phone number. versions: the app's or Home Assistant's version.

port.description: Only when it isn't the usual port for the protocol.

source.description: Where the connection starts: Home Assistant itself, or the browser showing the dashboard.

run_by_name.description: The name of whoever runs the server, such as a company or a town.

network.description: Where the server is: on the user's home network, on the internet, or either one, depending on the user's setup.

encrypted.description: Whether the connection is encrypted (https, wss, TLS). setting: a setting decides, named in encryption_setting.

encryption_setting.description: The setting that turns encryption on, as users see it or write it.

when.description: always: whenever the app runs. setting: only when a setting turns it on. user_action: only when a person does something, such as opening a popup.

setting.description: The setting's name as users see it or write it.

condition.description: The exact condition in words, when it's more than one setting.

on_by_default.description: true when the setting that turns this connection on is on out of the box.

protection.description: What stands in for the Home Assistant login. none: nothing, anyone who can reach Home Assistant gets an answer. own_token: the app checks a token of its own. signed_link: a link Home Assistant signed. webhook: a Home Assistant webhook id.

local_only.description: true when it only answers on the local network.

checks.description: What the app checks itself before it answers.

sent_to.description: The hosts it goes to. setup_address: the address the user entered at setup.

kind.description: long_lived: a long-lived access token. refresh: a refresh token, which can make new access tokens. access: a short-lived access token. dashboard_session: the token of the person using the dashboard, which a card can read in the browser.

admin_user.description: true when the token belongs to an administrator.

lifetime.description: How long the token lasts, such as "30 minutes" or "365 days".

given_to.description: Where the token goes outside Home Assistant. setup_address: the address the user entered at setup. An empty list says it stays in Home Assistant, or in the browser for a dashboard_session.

uses.description: secrets_file: reads secrets.yaml. other_apps_settings: reads other integrations' options. other_apps_credentials: reads other integrations' stored passwords, tokens or keys. user_list: reads the list of users. change_users: adds, changes or removes users. login_store: reads Home Assistant's login store. storage_files: reads or writes files in .storage directly. supervisor_api: calls the Supervisor API. location_history: reads location history for many entities at once. patches_home_assistant: replaces or wraps Home Assistant's own code while it runs. actions: runs actions on entities that aren't its own, or actions that change Home Assistant itself, listed in actions.

actions.description: The actions, such as lock.unlock on any lock, or homeassistant.restart.

kind.description: service_key: a key for a service the developer runs.

contents.description: What's in a report, and how often it's sent.

on_by_default.description: true when it's on out of the box.

setting.description: The setting that turns it on or off.

built_from.description: Where its source code is, such as a repository or a file in one.

built_by.description: ci: a public build workflow made it. developer: the developer built it on their own machine.

destination.description: The host or URL it comes from.

setting.description: The setting's name, when destination_set_by is setting.

pinned.description: true when the app asks for one exact version or checks a checksum.
